source_refs.note: Practice long questions written from Unit 11 (PDF 288-298, printed 286-296); not printed in the book. Based on the unit's text, theorems, formulas and worked examples (changed values); none repeats the unit's exercises. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice long questions for the whole of Unit 11 (Vector Valued Functions and Their Derivatives (TOC: '...and Their Differentiations')), in the shape of a Board Section-II question part: each carries 5 marks (a longer problem, a proof or a derivation). Each one is solved in full, step by step.

blocks.prompt: 1 A stone is thrown from the origin with initial speed \(v_{0} = 49\) m/s at \(60^{\circ}\) above the horizontal; \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^{2}\), air resistance ignored. (i) Construct its position vector \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) with its domain. (ii) Find how far from the origin it lands. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use the three steps: horizontal component at constant speed, vertical component with gravity, then the time interval in the air.
steps: Domain: \(y = t(24.5\sqrt{3} - 4.9t) = 0 \Rightarrow t = 0\) or \(t = \dfrac{24.5\sqrt{3}}{4.9} = 5\sqrt{3}\), so \(0 \le t \le 5\sqrt{3} \approx 8.66\) s

blocks.prompt: 2 A ball is kicked from the origin with \(v_{0} = 20\) m/s at \(45^{\circ}\) (\(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^{2}\)). Construct \(\mathbf{r}(t)\), eliminate \(t\) to find the equation of its path, and use it to find where it lands and its greatest height. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write the components, solve the x-component for t and substitute in the y-component; the path is a downward parabola.
steps: \(y = x - 4.9 \cdot \dfrac{x^{2}}{200} = x - 0.0245x^{2}\), a parabola opening downward
Greatest height at the middle \(x = \dfrac{1000}{49}\): \(y = \dfrac{1000}{49} - 0.0245\left(\dfrac{1000}{49}\right)^{2} = \dfrac{1000}{49} - \dfrac{500}{49} = \dfrac{500}{49} \approx 10.2\) m
blocks.final_answer: Path \(y = x - 0.0245x^{2}\); lands at \(x = \dfrac{2000}{49} \approx 40.8\) m; greatest height \(\dfrac{500}{49} \approx 10.2\) m

blocks.prompt: 3 A camera drone follows \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 6\cos t\,\hat{i} + 6\sin t\,\hat{j} + 0.8t\,\hat{k}\), \(t \ge 0\) (metres, seconds). (i) Show that it always stays 6 m from the \(z\)-axis. (ii) Find its climb per turn. (iii) Find its position at \(t = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\) and after three full turns. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Look at the x- and y-components together (circle), then the z-component alone (steady climb).

book_ref.quote: represents the steady ascent at 0.5 meters per second

steps: \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 36\cos^{2}t + 36\sin^{2}t = 36\), so the distance from the \(z\)-axis is \(\sqrt{36} = 6\) m
One turn: \(t\) grows by \(2\pi\); climb \(= 0.8 \times 2\pi = 1.6\pi \approx 5.03\) m
So after three turns it is at \((6, 0, 4.8\pi) \approx (6, 0, 15.08)\), directly above the start \((6, 0, 0)\)

blocks.prompt: 4 Find the domain of \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \ln(t - 1)\,\hat{i} + \sqrt{6 - t}\,\hat{j} + \dfrac{1}{t^{2} - 9}\,\hat{k}\). Hence decide whether \(\mathbf{r}(2)\), \(\mathbf{r}(3)\) and \(\mathbf{r}(6)\) exist, and find those that do. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Find where each component is defined, then keep only the values of t that work for all three.

blocks.prompt: 5 Find the domain and range of \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \sqrt{9 - t^{2}}\,\hat{i} + \dfrac{1}{t + 2}\,\hat{j}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Domain of each component, then the intersection; find each component's values only over that domain, piece by piece; the range is the set of output points.

book_ref.quote: Find the intersection of the domains of each component

steps: \(x(t)\): \(t^{2}\) runs over \([0, 9]\) on the domain, so \(x = \sqrt{9 - t^{2}} \in [0, 3]\)
\(y(t)\): \(-3 \le t < -2 \Rightarrow -1 \le t + 2 < 0 \Rightarrow y \le -1\); \(-2 < t \le 3 \Rightarrow 0 < t + 2 \le 5 \Rightarrow y \ge \dfrac{1}{5}\)

Range: the points \(\left\langle\sqrt{9 - t^{2}}, \dfrac{1}{t + 2}\right\rangle\), \(t\) in the domain; with \(t = \dfrac{1}{y} - 2\) these are \(\left(\sqrt{9 - \left(\dfrac{1}{y} - 2\right)^{2}},\ y\right)\), \(y \le -1\) or \(y \ge \dfrac{1}{5}\)
Check: \(t = -3 \to (0, -1)\), \(t = 0 \to \left(3, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\), \(t = 3 \to \left(0, \dfrac{1}{5}\right)\); \(y = -\dfrac{1}{2}\) would need \(t = -4\), outside the domain
blocks.final_answer: Domain \([-3, -2) \cup (-2, 3]\); range: the points \(\left(\sqrt{9 - t^{2}}, \dfrac{1}{t + 2}\right)\) of the curve, with \(x \in [0, 3]\) and \(y \in (-\infty, -1] \cup \left[\dfrac{1}{5}, \infty\right)\)

blocks.prompt: 6 Find the domain and range of \(\mathbf{r}(t) = (2t - 1)\,\hat{i} + \sqrt{t}\,\hat{j}\), and describe the range as a curve. Is \((7, 2)\) in the range? Is \((7, -2)\)? (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Find the domain from the square root, then eliminate t to see which curve the output points lie on.

book_ref.quote: Determine the domain of each component separately.

steps: \(2t - 1\) is defined for all \(t\); \(\sqrt{t}\) needs \(t \ge 0\). Domain: \([0, \infty)\)
Range: the upper half (\(y \ge 0\)) of the parabola \(x = 2y^{2} - 1\), starting at \((-1, 0)\)
\((7, 2)\): \(t = 4\) gives \(x = 7\), \(y = 2\): yes. \((7, -2)\): \(y = \sqrt{t}\) is never negative: no

blocks.prompt: 7 Starting from \(\mathbf{r}'(t) = \displaystyle\lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \dfrac{\mathbf{r}(t + \Delta t) - \mathbf{r}(t)}{\Delta t}\), show that \(\mathbf{r}'(t) = f_{1}'(t)\,\hat{i} + f_{2}'(t)\,\hat{j} + f_{3}'(t)\,\hat{k}\) for \(\mathbf{r}(t) = f_{1}(t)\,\hat{i} + f_{2}(t)\,\hat{j} + f_{3}(t)\,\hat{k}\). Verify it from the definition for \(\mathbf{r}(t) = t^{2}\,\hat{i} + t^{3}\,\hat{j}\) at \(t = 1\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write the difference quotient component by component; the unit vectors are constants, so the limit acts on each component.

book_ref.quote: If the limit exists, then \(\mathbf{r}'(t)\) is computed by differentiating each component:

steps: \(\mathbf{r}(t + \Delta t) - \mathbf{r}(t) = [f_{1}(t + \Delta t) - f_{1}(t)]\,\hat{i} + [f_{2}(t + \Delta t) - f_{2}(t)]\,\hat{j} + [f_{3}(t + \Delta t) - f_{3}(t)]\,\hat{k}\)
Divide by \(\Delta t\): each bracket becomes \(\dfrac{f_{n}(t + \Delta t) - f_{n}(t)}{\Delta t}\), \(n = 1, 2, 3\); \(\hat{i}, \hat{j}, \hat{k}\) are constant
Let \(\Delta t \to 0\): each quotient tends to \(f_{n}'(t)\), so \(\mathbf{r}'(t) = f_{1}'(t)\,\hat{i} + f_{2}'(t)\,\hat{j} + f_{3}'(t)\,\hat{k}\) (when every \(f_{n}'\) exists)
For \(t^{2}\,\hat{i} + t^{3}\,\hat{j}\) at \(t = 1\): \(\dfrac{(1 + \Delta t)^{2} - 1}{\Delta t} = 2 + \Delta t\), \(\dfrac{(1 + \Delta t)^{3} - 1}{\Delta t} = 3 + 3\Delta t + (\Delta t)^{2}\)
Limit: \(\mathbf{r}'(1) = 2\,\hat{i} + 3\,\hat{j}\); by components \(\mathbf{r}'(t) = 2t\,\hat{i} + 3t^{2}\,\hat{j}\) also gives \(2\,\hat{i} + 3\,\hat{j}\) at \(t = 1\)

blocks.prompt: 8 Find \(\mathbf{r}'(t)\) and \(\mathbf{r}'(0)\) for \(\mathbf{r}(t) = e^{t}\cos t\,\hat{i} + \dfrac{t}{1 + t^{2}}\,\hat{j} + \sqrt{2t + 1}\,\hat{k}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Differentiate each component with the right rule (product, quotient, chain), then substitute t = 0.

book_ref.quote: is computed by differentiating each component

steps: Product rule: \((e^{t}\cos t)' = e^{t}\cos t - e^{t}\sin t = e^{t}(\cos t - \sin t)\)

blocks.explanation: Differentiate each component in general with the chain rule, then put t = pi/6.

book_ref.quote: first differentiate each component in general, then substitute

blocks.prompt: 10 A part on a sorting machine has position \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 2t^{2}\,\hat{i} + 3\cos t\,\hat{j}\) (metres, seconds). At \(t = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\) find its velocity, acceleration, speed and direction of motion, and say whether it is speeding up or slowing down. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Differentiate once for v and twice for a in general, then substitute; speed = |v|, direction = v/|v|, and the sign of v . a decides speeding up or slowing down.

book_ref.quote: the derivative of the velocity vector with respect to time

blocks.prompt: 11 A drone inspects a chimney along \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 4\cos t\,\hat{i} + 4\sin t\,\hat{j} + 3t\,\hat{k}\) (metres, seconds). At \(t = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\) find (i) velocity (ii) acceleration (iii) speed (iv) direction of motion. Show that the acceleration points towards the chimney's axis (the \(z\)-axis) and that the speed is not changing. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Differentiate component by component, then substitute; compare a with the drone's position to see where it points.

book_ref.quote: the direction only (the unit tangent vector)

steps: Position \(\mathbf{r}\!\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = (0, 4, 1.5\pi)\): \(-4\,\hat{j}\) points from \(y = 4\) back to the \(z\)-axis; \(\mathbf{v} \cdot \mathbf{a} = 0 + 0 + 0 = 0\), so the speed is not changing

blocks.prompt: 12 A particle moves on \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 3\cos t\,\hat{i} + 2\sin t\,\hat{j}\). (i) Show that its path is the ellipse \(\dfrac{x^{2}}{9} + \dfrac{y^{2}}{4} = 1\). (ii) Show that \(\mathbf{a}(t) = -\mathbf{r}(t)\). (iii) Find where on the path the speed is greatest and least. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use cos^2 + sin^2 = 1 for the path; differentiate twice for a; write the speed squared in terms of sin^2 t only.

book_ref.quote: is the acceleration of the particle, denoted by

steps: \(\mathbf{v} = -3\sin t\,\hat{i} + 2\cos t\,\hat{j}\), \(\mathbf{a} = -3\cos t\,\hat{i} - 2\sin t\,\hat{j} = -(3\cos t\,\hat{i} + 2\sin t\,\hat{j}) = -\mathbf{r}(t)\): the acceleration always points to the origin
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\mathbf{a} = -\mathbf{r}\); greatest speed \(3\) at \((0, \pm 2)\), least speed \(2\) at \((\pm 3, 0)\)

blocks.prompt: 13 For \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 5\cos 2t\,\hat{i} + 5\sin 2t\,\hat{j}\), show that (i) the speed is constant, (ii) \(\mathbf{a}(t) = -4\,\mathbf{r}(t)\), (iii) \(\mathbf{v} \perp \mathbf{a}\) at every \(t\), and (iv) \(|\mathbf{a}| = \dfrac{(\text{speed})^{2}}{\text{radius}}\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Differentiate with the chain rule (factor 2 each time), then use sin^2 + cos^2 = 1 and the dot product.

blocks.prompt: 14 For \(\mathbf{r}(t) = x(t)\,\hat{i} + y(t)\,\hat{j} + z(t)\,\hat{k}\), show that \(\dfrac{d}{dt}|\mathbf{v}|^{2} = 2\,\mathbf{v} \cdot \mathbf{a}\). Use it to show that the particle on \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 2\cos 3t\,\hat{i} + 2\sin 3t\,\hat{j} + 5t\,\hat{k}\) moves with constant speed, and find that speed. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write |v|^2 as a sum of squares of the velocity components and differentiate with the chain rule.
steps: \(\mathbf{v} \cdot \mathbf{a} = 108\sin 3t\cos 3t - 108\sin 3t\cos 3t + 0 = 0\), so \(\dfrac{d}{dt}|\mathbf{v}|^{2} = 0\) and the speed is constant
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\dfrac{d}{dt}|\mathbf{v}|^{2} = 2\,\mathbf{v} \cdot \mathbf{a}\); for the helix \(\mathbf{v} \cdot \mathbf{a} = 0\), constant speed \(\sqrt{61}\)

blocks.prompt: 15 A ball moves with \(\mathbf{r}(t) = 12t\,\hat{i} + (19.6t - 4.9t^{2})\,\hat{j}\) (metres, seconds). Find (i) the time of flight (ii) the time and value of the greatest height (iii) the horizontal distance covered (iv) the velocity and speed when it lands. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use y = 0 for landing; at the highest point the vertical velocity is zero; the velocity is the derivative of r.

book_ref.quote: represent the velocity vector of the particle, which is tangent to the curve

steps: \(y = t(19.6 - 4.9t) = 0 \Rightarrow t = 0\) or \(t = 4\): time of flight \(4\) s

blocks.prompt: 16 A particle moves with \(\mathbf{r}(t) = (t^{3} - 3t^{2})\,\hat{i} + (2t^{2} - 8t)\,\hat{j}\), \(t \ge 0\). (i) When is it at rest, and where? (ii) Find its speed at \(t = 1\) and \(t = 3\), and say whether it is speeding up or slowing down at each. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: At rest means v = 0 (both components zero together); use the sign of v . a for speeding up or slowing down.

book_ref.quote: how fast and which way it moves (tangent to the path)

blocks.final_answer: (i) at rest at \(t = 2\), at \((-4, -8)\) (ii) \(t = 1\): speed \(5\), slowing down; \(t = 3\): speed \(\sqrt{97}\), speeding up

blocks.prompt: 17 A particle moves with \(\mathbf{r}(t) = e^{t}\cos t\,\hat{i} + e^{t}\sin t\,\hat{j}\). (i) Show that its speed is \(\sqrt{2}\,e^{t}\). (ii) At \(t = 0\) find its velocity, acceleration and direction of motion, and say whether it is speeding up. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use the product rule on each component; expand the squares for the speed.

book_ref.quote: how fast and which way it moves (tangent to the path)

steps: \(\mathbf{v} = e^{t}(\cos t - \sin t)\,\hat{i} + e^{t}(\sin t + \cos t)\,\hat{j}\)
\(|\mathbf{v}|^{2} = e^{2t}[(\cos t - \sin t)^{2} + (\sin t + \cos t)^{2}] = e^{2t}(2) \Rightarrow |\mathbf{v}| = \sqrt{2}\,e^{t}\)
\(\mathbf{a} = e^{t}(\cos t - \sin t - \sin t - \cos t)\,\hat{i} + e^{t}(\sin t + \cos t + \cos t - \sin t)\,\hat{j} = -2e^{t}\sin t\,\hat{i} + 2e^{t}\cos t\,\hat{j}\)

blocks.prompt: 18 A robot's gripper moves with \(\mathbf{r}(t) = t^{2}\,\hat{i} + 2t\,\hat{j} + \ln t\,\hat{k}\), \(t > 0\). At \(t = 1\) find its velocity, acceleration, speed and direction of motion, and say whether it is speeding up or slowing down. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Differentiate each component twice, substitute t = 1, then use |v|, v/|v| and the sign of v . a.

book_ref.quote: how fast it moves, without direction
